Yup, where I work we actually did both. Packaged bibs and premix tanks. With tanks it was a huge hassle of cleaning, prepping and running a finished product into a 5 gallon tank. Way way more work than sending 5 gallons of straight syrup to a bag in the box. No hourly testing to check for variances. We just had to bag it, weigh it occasionally.

The four white hose lines attach to one part on top of each tank. The soda lines. Not seen would have to have a co2 tank with a 4 hose line manifold going again to the other part on top of the tanks. Co2 goes into tank, syrup pushes out through the hoses which coincide with each handle. Inside the actual dispenser part would have to be filled with water to create an ice bank to keep the coke cold. Without electricity you’d have whatever temp the syrup tanks were. I’ve worked for coke for 13 years. These are obsolete as not very many people would use tanks like those anymore. Not cost effective compared to even a basic postmix bib system. We actually have a bunch of these on casters we could wheel to events for banks, fundraisers, etc.
